chapter: Records, Blanton, the Chicago scene, Nat Cole and Nadine
title: The band whose reed men doubled on violin, and Chick Webb's flutes
summary: A story of an Earl Hines band that lost its reed section in a car wreck, and Chick Webb's saxophones playing flutes.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Well, did they tell you -- did Earl Hines ever tell you about the band that he had, that they had a big automobile wreck, and all of the reed section played violins?
No. What is -- is playing the violin related to the automobile accident? Wait a minute. Tell me the story.
Wait a minute now, let me see. Yeah, it was Earl's band. I was thinking maybe it was Earl Fletcher. It was Earl's band.
All of the violins, all of the reed men, doubled on violin.
Do you remember who those reed men were?

Well, I remember Omar Simeon, but I don't know whether -- if he was with the band at that time. Darnell Howard, I remember. I don't know if he was with the band. I think he was a replacement for some of these fellows because they got killed in the accident, you know?
You mean, there was an accident and he lost his whole saxophone section?

Well, the majority of them. And at that same time, Chick Webb, he was playing at a saxophone section where all of them played flutes. In the early 30's, Chick Webb and his Chickadees. So flute's nothing new today. They played, too. Legitimately, they played. Yeah, that all -- yeah.
